DGGRID’s native clipping accurate offers options exposed R: clip_subset_type = GDAL — clip using arbitrary GDAL vector polygon file, proper polygon-intersection testing (clip_type = POLY_INTERSECT), polygon hole support (clip_using_holes), geodetic densification clipping edges (geodetic_densify). clip_subset_type = COARSE_CELLS — specify list cell addresses coarser resolution define region. supported hexagon grids. title: DGGRID v9.0b — Features Not Exposed in the R Package Version 4.0.0
text: Status: Implemented via DgDiscTopoRFS public API (HIERNDX address type). C++ path: - dgchildren → GetChildren() constructs GridThing res+1 (idggs covers res+2 levels) → GridThing::getChildrenAt(seqnum, parentRes) → DgDiscTopoRFS::setAllChildren(parentRes, loc, vec) → DgHexIDGGS::setAddAllChildren() (interior + boundary children). - dgparent → GetParent() → GridThing::getParentAt(seqnum, childRes) → DgDiscTopoRFS::setParents(childRes, loc, vec) → DgHexIDGGS::setAddParents(). Design note — boundary children: setAddAllChildren returns interior children (1 per aperture-3 parent, 3 aperture-4) plus boundary children shared neighboring cells. boundary child’s primary parent (returned setParents) may neighbor, original parent. R-level test reflects : (prnt$parent == parent_cell) rather (...). Remaining gaps: - immediate children (one resolution step) supported; multi-step children require iterative calls. - HEXAGON topology supported (dgverify-level check); DIAMOND TRIANGLE . - HIERNDX address system (Z7/ZOrder/Z3) still exposed coordinate conversions; dgchildren/dgparent use SEQNUM-based DgDiscTopoRFS public API instead.

title: DGGRID v9.0b — Features Not Exposed in the R Package Version 4.0.0
text: Status: Implemented. dgearthgrid(dggs, densify=N) dgcellstogrid(dggs, cells, densify=N) add N extra vertices along cell edge (default 0). Threaded DgParams::densify → GlobalGridGenerator / SeqNumGridGenerator → dgg.setVertices(*loc, verts, densify). Remaining gaps: None core feature. DGGRID supports values 0–500; R passes integer without clamping (--range values produce C++ error).

code: #Include libraries library(dggridR)  N <- 100    #How many cells to sample  #Distribute the points uniformly on a sphere using equations from #http://mathworld.wolfram.com/SpherePointPicking.html u     <- runif(N) v     <- runif(N) theta <- 2*pi*u      * 180/pi phi   <- acos(2*v-1) * 180/pi lon   <- theta-180 lat   <- phi-90  df    <- data.frame(lat=lat,lon=lon)  #Construct a global grid in which every hexagonal cell has an area of #100,000 miles^2. You could, of course, choose a much smaller value, but these #will show up when I map them later.  #Note: Cells can only have certain areas, the `dgconstruct()` function below #will tell you which area is closest to the one you want. You can also round #up or down.  #Note: 12 cells are actually pentagons with an area 5/6 that of the hexagons #But, with millions and millions of hexes, you are unlikely to choose one #Future versions of the package will make it easier to reject the pentagons dggs    <- dgconstruct(area=100000, metric=FALSE, resround='nearest')  #Get the corresponding grid cells for each randomly chosen lat-long df$cell <- dgGEO_to_SEQNUM(dggs,df$lon,df$lat)$seqnum  #Get the hexes for each of these cells gridfilename <- dgcellstogrid(dggs,df$cell) #Get the grid in a more convenient format grid <- dgcellstogrid(dggs,df$cell) grid <- st_wrap_dateline(grid, options = c("WRAPDATELINE=YES","DATELINEOFFSET=180"), quiet = TRUE)  #Get polygons for each country of the world countries <- map_data("world")  #Plot everything on a flat map p <- ggplot() +     geom_polygon(data=countries, aes(x=long, y=lat, group=group), fill=NA, color="black")   +     geom_sf(data=grid, fill=alpha("green", alpha=0.4), color=alpha("white", alpha=0.4)) p

title: dggridR: Discrete Global Grids for R
text: dgpoints_to_cells() maps set lon/lat points grid cells returns grid geometry sf object, optionally count column showing many points fell cell. dgbin_points() skips geometry returns plain data frame per-cell statistics (count, mean, total).  dgbin_points() useful need aggregated numbers rather geometry:
code: library(dggridR)  data(dgquakes) dggs <- dgconstruct(spacing = 1000, metric = FALSE, resround = 'down')  # One step: points → sf grid with per-cell counts grid <- dgpoints_to_cells(dggs, dgquakes$lon, dgquakes$lat, return_count = TRUE) grid$count <- log(grid$count)  countries <- map_data("world") wrapped   <- st_wrap_dateline(grid, options = c("WRAPDATELINE=YES","DATELINEOFFSET=180"), quiet = TRUE) ggplot() +     geom_polygon(data=countries, aes(x=long, y=lat, group=group), fill=NA, color="black") +     geom_sf(data=wrapped, aes(fill=count), color=alpha("white", 0.4)) +     scale_fill_gradient(low="blue", high="red") +     ggtitle("Earthquakes per cell (log scale)") bins <- dgbin_points(dggs, dgquakes$lon, dgquakes$lat, output_count = TRUE) head(bins) ##   seqnum count ## 1      1     1 ## 2      2   701 ## 3      4    35 ## 4      5   257 ## 5      7    68 ## 6      8   190

title: dggridR: Discrete Global Grids for R
text: dgneighbors() returns 6 adjacent cells hexagonal cell (supported triangular grids).
code: library(dggridR)  dggs <- dgconstruct(res = 2, show_info = FALSE)  center_cell <- 30 nbrs <- dgneighbors(dggs, center_cell)  # Visualise the cell and its ring of neighbours all_cells <- c(center_cell, nbrs$neighbor) grid      <- dgcellstogrid(dggs, all_cells) grid$role <- ifelse(grid$seqnum == center_cell, "centre", "neighbour") ggplot() +     geom_sf(data=grid, aes(fill=role), color="white") +     scale_fill_manual(values = c(centre = "#E41A1C", neighbour = "#377EB8")) +     ggtitle(paste("Cell", center_cell, "and its 6 neighbours"))

title: dggridR: Discrete Global Grids for R
text: dgchildren() returns cells next finer resolution contained within input cell. dgparent() returns coarser-resolution cell contains input cell. require hexagonal grid.  Round-tripping via dgparent() confirms interior children map back parent (boundary children may shared neighbouring cell):
code: library(dggridR)  dggs_parent <- dgconstruct(res = 3, show_info = FALSE) dggs_child  <- dgconstruct(res = 4, show_info = FALSE)  parent_cell <- 100 chld <- dgchildren(dggs_parent, parent_cell)  # Visualise the parent boundary and its child cells grid_parent <- dgcellstogrid(dggs_parent, parent_cell) grid_child  <- dgcellstogrid(dggs_child, chld$child) ggplot() +     geom_sf(data=grid_child,  fill=alpha("#377EB8", 0.5), color="white") +     geom_sf(data=grid_parent, fill=NA, color="#E41A1C", linewidth=1.2) +     ggtitle(paste("Children of cell", parent_cell, "at res 4 (red = parent boundary)")) prnt <- dgparent(dggs_child, chld$child) head(prnt) ##   seqnum parent ## 1    297    100 ## 2    306    106 ## 3    307    111 ## 4    298    111 ## 5    288     97 ## 6    287    100

title: dggridR: Discrete Global Grids for R
text: densify parameter dgearthgrid() dgcellstogrid() inserts additional interpolated vertices along cell edge. default (densify=0) uses corner vertices; higher values add intermediate points produce smoother curves cells displayed curved projection.
code: library(dggridR)  dggs <- dgconstruct(res = 2, show_info = FALSE) g0   <- dgearthgrid(dggs, densify = 0)  # corners only g5   <- dgearthgrid(dggs, densify = 5)  # 5 extra vertices per edge # Vertex counts increase substantially with densification c(   sparse = sum(lengths(lapply(sf::st_geometry(g0), sf::st_coordinates))),   dense  = sum(lengths(lapply(sf::st_geometry(g5), sf::st_coordinates))) ) ## sparse  dense  ##   2528  13328

title: dggridR: Discrete Global Grids for R
text: default 12 pentagonal cells placed fixed, ---way locations. Pass orient = "RANDOM" dgconstruct() uniformly random icosahedral orientation, useful sensitivity analyses Monte Carlo studies. Use set.seed() call reproducibility.
code: library(dggridR)  set.seed(42) dggs_r <- dgconstruct(res = 3, orient = "RANDOM", show_info = FALSE) gr     <- dgearthgrid(dggs_r) countries <- map_data("world") ggplot() +     geom_polygon(data=countries, aes(x=long, y=lat, group=group), fill=NA, color="black") +     geom_sf(data=gr, fill=NA, color=alpha("#1B9E77", 0.5)) +     ggtitle("ISEA3H res-3 grid with random orientation (set.seed(42))")

title: Discrete Global Grids for R — dggridR-package
text: dggridR provides discrete global grids (DGGs) — spatial binning surface Earth using equal-area hexagonal, triangular, diamond cells. Unlike rectangular grids, DGG cells area regardless location, making ideal spatial statistics, point aggregation, multi-scale analysis. package wraps DGGRID v9.0b C++ engine via Rcpp. Grid Construction dgconstruct() — Build DGG specification (projection, topology, aperture, resolution)dgsetres() — Change resolution existing DGG specificationdgverify() — Validate DGG specification Grid Information dginfo() — Print human-readable summary DGG specificationdggetres() — Return table cell counts, areas, spacings resolutionsdgmaxcell() — Return maximum cell ID given resolutiondg_closest_res_to_area() — Select resolution target cell areadg_closest_res_to_spacing() — Select resolution target inter-cell spacingdg_closest_res_to_cls() — Select resolution target characteristic length scale Grid Materialization dgearthgrid() — Generate full global grid sf objectdgcellstogrid() — Generate grid cell boundaries specified cell IDsdgrectgrid() — Generate grid covering lat/lon bounding boxdgshptogrid() — Generate grid covering shapefile sf polygon Point Aggregation dgpoints_to_cells() — Map lon/lat points grid cells; returns sf grid optional per-cell countsdgbin_points() — Aggregate numeric values cell; returns per-cell count, mean, /total Cell Relationships dgneighbors() — Return adjacent cell IDs input cell (hexagonal grids)dgchildren() — Return child cell IDs next finer resolutiondgparent() — Return parent cell ID next coarser resolution Coordinate Conversion Thirty functions convert five cell address systems supported DGGRID, named dgINPUT_to_OUTPUT: GEO (geographic lon/lat), SEQNUM (globally unique integer cell ID), Q2DI (quad-based integer), Q2DD (quad-based double), PROJTRI (projected triangle). commonly used : dgGEO_to_SEQNUM() — Geographic coordinates cell sequence numberdgSEQNUM_to_GEO() — Cell sequence number geographic coordinates Data dgquakes — Lat/lon locations 1,000 earthquakes Fiji (datasets package)dg_shpfname_south_africa() — Path bundled South Africa border shapefile

text: recommended default grid ISEA3H (Icosahedral Snyder Equal Area, aperture 3, hexagonal), constructed dgconstruct(projection = "ISEA", topology = "HEXAGON", aperture = 3). Every resolution contains exactly 12 pentagonal cells (area 5/6 hexagon); default orientation placed ---way locations. Use orient = "RANDOM" dgconstruct() uniformly random icosahedral orientation. Retained mitigations earlier attempts: disable RCPP_USE_GLOBAL_ROSTREAM RcppExports.cpp enforce via src/Makevars (-URCPP_USE_GLOBAL_ROSTREAM); remove DgConverterBase::traceStream_ dgcout fallback; exclude test.cpp package shared-library build. Fixed install warnings signed/unsigned comparisons DgDiscRFSGrids.h DgZ3StringRF.cpp. Guarded MSVC-#pragma comment(lib, ...) safileio.c avoid GCC unknown pragma warnings. Fixed integer truncation warnings replacing C abs() std::abs() long long arguments DGGRID headers. Added durable patch steps update_from_upstream.sh fixes survive source regeneration.

title: dggridR 4.1.0
text: dgconstruct() gains aperture = 7 ISEA7H / FULLER7H hexagonal grids. dgconstruct() gains aperture_type = "MIXED43" num_aperture_4_res ISEA43H / FULLER43H mixed-aperture grids. dgconstruct() gains orient = "RANDOM" uniformly random icosahedral orientation (reproducible via set.seed()). New dgneighbors(dggs, cells) returns adjacent cell IDs input cell (hexagonal grids ). New dgchildren(dggs, cells) returns child cell IDs next finer resolution. New dgparent(dggs, cells) returns parent cell ID next coarser resolution. New dgpoints_to_cells(dggs, lon, lat) maps lon/lat points grid cells returns sf grid optional per-cell counts. New dgbin_points(dggs, lon, lat, values) aggregates point data grid cells, returning per-cell count, mean, /total data frame. dgearthgrid() dgcellstogrid() gain densify parameter insert extra vertices along cell edges smoother boundaries. dgearthgrid() dgcellstogrid() now materialize sf polygon grids native C implementation using R’s C API, preserving DGGRID ring order avoiding previous s2/collapse polygon construction path. text: CRAN release: 2024-07-26 Fixed numeric precision issue Apple Silicon (#63). Removed dplyr, rlang, sp dependencies; added collapse s2 (zero additional transitive dependencies), yielding significant performance gains especially grid materialization. dgshptogrid() now accepts sf object memory addition shapefile path. dgcellstogrid(), dgearthgrid(), dgrectgrid(), dgshptogrid() gain return_sf = TRUE; setting return_sf = FALSE returns memory-efficient long data frame cell-vertex coordinates.
